backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first ~300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value from the step counter each iteration and writing it into the Muon param-group before the step. Leave all other optimizer settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3. Since training is a fixed 300 s wall-clock budget, the cheaper orthogonalization should yield more optimizer steps. Keep the NS coefficients and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon

backlog.spec: Scale each Muon orthogonalized update by 0.2 * sqrt(max(rows, cols)) instead of the current shape-based factor, so the update RMS matches AdamW's typical RMS. Then set the Muon LR to be shared with the AdamW-scale convention: retune MATRIX_LR to roughly 0.02 and keep WEIGHT_DECAY as the decoupled Muon weight decay. Make this the only change in the update rule.
backlog.title: Moonlight-style Muon update RMS scaling

backlog.spec: Add decoupled weight decay of 0.01 (multiplied by the Adam LR, AdamW-style) to the embedding, lm_head and per-layer scalar parameters, which are currently updated by Adam without weight decay. Matrix parameters keep the existing Muon weight decay. This is a single added decay term in the Adam step.
backlog.title: Decoupled weight decay on Adam-managed parameters

backlog.spec: Use Adam betas (0.9, 0.95) for the token-embedding and lm_head parameter groups while keeping ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.95) for the per-layer scalars. This changes only the betas passed to those two Adam param-groups.
backlog.title: Lower beta1 for embedding and lm_head Adam groups

backlog.spec: Make the Muon weight decay coefficient a function of training progress: start at WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 and decrease linearly to 0.0 at the end of the time budget, using the same progress fraction that drives the LR schedule. Apply it to the Muon param-groups each step.
backlog.title: Linearly decay Muon weight decay to zero

backlog.spec: Turn off the Nesterov look-ahead in the Muon momentum update so the update uses the plain momentum buffer. Everything else, including the momentum coefficient and orthogonalization, stays the same. This isolates whether the Nesterov variant helps at this scale.
backlog.title: Disable Nesterov momentum in Muon

backlog.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown after the constant phase with a cosine decay: multiplier = 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi * p)) where p runs from 0 to 1 across the warmdown window (the last WARMDOWN_RATIO of the time budget). The constant phase and the peak LRs are unchanged.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the final 70% of the time budget instead of 50%. Keep the linear shape and all other hyperparameters the same.
backlog.title: Longer warmdown window

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from 0 to its peak over the first 2% of the time budget (about 6 s) before the constant phase. Use the same time-based progress variable as the existing schedule.
backlog.title: Short linear LR warmup

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the warmdown ends at 10% of each group's peak LR instead of decaying to zero. This keeps some learning signal at the end of the run; no other change.
backlog.title: Non-zero final LR fraction

backlog.spec: Keep the token-embedding and lm_head Adam learning rates at their peak values for the whole run, applying the warmdown multiplier only to the Muon matrix and scalar parameter groups. This makes the warmdown apply only to the parameters that benefit most from annealing.
backlog.title: Hold embedding LR constant through warmdown

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (~262K tokens per step), so the same 300 s budget yields about twice as many optimizer steps. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64 and let gradient accumulation halve automatically. Leave LRs unchanged.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch of 2^18 tokens

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20 (~1M tokens per step) and scale the Adam LRs (EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR, SCALAR_LR) by sqrt(2) and MATRIX_LR by sqrt(2) as well. This tests whether fewer, less noisy steps beat more steps within the fixed budget.
backlog.title: Larger batch 2^20 with sqrt LR scaling

backlog.spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 and linearly increase the effective batch (via gradient accumulation steps) to 2**19 over the first 40% of the time budget, then hold it. Round accumulation steps to an integer and keep LRs unchanged. Early steps are cheap and numerous, later steps are larger and less noisy.
backlog.title: Batch-size ramp from 2^17 to 2^19

backlog.spec: Replace the squared-ReLU MLP in each block with a SwiGLU MLP: two up-projections to hidden size round(2/3 * 4 * model_dim) gated by SiLU, then a down-projection. Keep the parameter count close to the baseline by using that hidden width. Applies to all layers.
backlog.title: SwiGLU MLP

backlog.spec: Apply logit soft-capping to the final output logits before the cross-entropy: logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15). Use the same cap for training loss and evaluation logits so the metric path is consistent; do not change the evaluation call itself.
backlog.title: Logit soft-capping

backlog.spec: Apply RMSNorm to queries and keys inside attention (if not already present) and give each head a learnable scalar gain on q and k initialized to 1. The gains are trained with the scalar Adam group. This controls attention logit scale without a fixed temperature.
backlog.title: Per-head learnable QK-norm gain

backlog.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48, so model_dim = 480 (rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM for head count) while total parameter count stays near the baseline. Keep WINDOW_PATTERN consistent with the new depth.
backlog.title: Deeper, narrower model

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SL" so every other layer uses full context and the rest use half context. This spends more attention compute on global context at the same depth. Keep all other settings the same.
backlog.title: Alternating SL window pattern

backlog.spec: Initialize each block's residual branch scale to 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH) and add a learned per-layer mix that blends the normalized input embedding x0 back into the residual stream before each block (x = a_l * x + b_l * x0 with a_l, b_l scalars in the scalar Adam group). This stabilizes deeper residual streams.
backlog.title: Learned residual scales with x0 skip mixing

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block to the parallel form x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), sharing a single pre-norm for both branches. This reduces sequential kernel launches per layer and may increase throughput within the fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP block

backlog.spec: Increase the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 so position frequencies vary more slowly across the context window. Keep head dimension and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Larger RoPE base

backlog.spec: Use grouped-query attention where the number of key/value heads is half the number of query heads (each KV head shared by two query heads). This reduces K/V projection parameters and memory bandwidth, freeing time for more steps in the fixed budget.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with half the KV heads

backlog.spec: Add a z-loss term to the training objective: 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) computed over the vocabulary per token. This keeps the output logit normalizer near zero and reduces logit drift late in training. Add it only to the training loss, not the evaluation path.
backlog.title: Z-loss regularization on logits

backlog.spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after the backward pass and before the optimizer step, across all parameters. This guards against occasional large-gradient spikes at the high peak LRs used here. No other change.
backlog.title: Gradient norm clipping

backlog.spec: Add dropout with probability 0.02 on each residual branch output (after attention and after MLP) during training only, disabled at evaluation. The short run is probably under-fitting, so this is a small test of whether any regularization helps. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Light residual dropout

backlog.spec: Train with a shorter sequence length early and lengthen it later: use half the configured sequence length for the first 30% of the time budget and the full length afterwards. Keep tokens per step at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE by adjusting the number of sequences per micro-batch. The data loader interface stays the same.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Maintain an EMA of model parameters with decay 0.999 updated each optimizer step, and use the EMA weights for the final model state used in evaluation. Keep the training weights unchanged for the optimizer. Do not modify the evaluation call; only swap in the EMA weights before the existing evaluation code runs.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights

backlog.spec: Enable TF32 matmul and cuDNN benchmark mode at startup (torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True and torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True), and use the fused AdamW implementation where available for the Adam parameter groups. This targets throughput only; numerics should be essentially unchanged.
backlog.title: Enable fast matmul and fused kernels

backlog.spec: Since the metric is bits per byte, weight each target token's cross-entropy by its UTF-8 byte length (computed from the tokenizer's decoded string for each vocab id, precomputed once into a float tensor of length vocab_size). Loss = sum(w[target] * ce) / sum(w[target]) over the batch, so the gradient matches the bpb objective instead of per-token averaging. Keep the logged training loss in the same form. Do not change the evaluation call or the summary printing. If the tokenizer's byte lengths are not available through the already-imported names, fall back to weight 1 and skip the change.
backlog.title: Byte-weighted cross-entropy loss

backlog.spec: During training only, randomly skip each transformer block's residual branch (attention and MLP output added as zero) with a drop probability that rises linearly with depth, from 0 at layer 0 to 0.1 at the last layer. Rescale the surviving branch by 1/(1-p) so expected activations match. Disable all dropping in eval mode. This is a single-line gating inside the block forward; use one Bernoulli draw per sample per block. Keep the rest of the training loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Stochastic depth on residual blocks

backlog.spec: Following ResFormer-style value residuals, cache the value tensor V produced by the first attention layer and, in every later layer, replace V with lambda_l * V_current + (1 - lambda_l) * V_first, where lambda_l is a learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5 and registered as a scalar parameter in the Adam group that already holds the per-layer scalars. Apply after the value projection and before attention. No extra matmuls are added.
backlog.title: Value residual from first layer

backlog.spec: Add a per-head sigmoid gate on the attention output: compute g = sigmoid(Linear(x)) with a small bias-free linear from the normalized block input to n_heads outputs (one scalar per head per token), and multiply each head's attention output by g before the output projection. Initialize the gate weights to zero so the gate starts at 0.5 everywhere. Adds roughly n_heads*model_dim parameters per layer and no change to the MLP.
backlog.title: Sigmoid-gated attention output

backlog.spec: Share the key and value projection weights between adjacent layer pairs (layers 2k and 2k+1 use the same W_k and W_v; keep the query, output, and MLP projections separate per layer). This cuts attention parameters by about a quarter and frees parameter budget for the same wall-clock. Keep RoPE, QK-norm and the window pattern unchanged. Make sure the Muon optimizer groups still get the shared tensor exactly once so it is not double-registered.
backlog.title: Cross-layer key-value sharing in pairs

backlog.spec: Add one auxiliary objective that predicts the token two positions ahead: a single extra linear projection (initialized from the main lm_head weights) applied to the final hidden state, with cross-entropy against the t+2 target. Total loss = main CE + 0.2 * auxiliary CE, applied only during training. The auxiliary head is excluded from the evaluation forward pass so the reported model is unchanged. Keep the optimizer group assignment of the main lm_head.
backlog.title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary head

backlog.spec: Scale the Muon learning rate for each transformer block's matrix parameters by a factor that decreases linearly with depth: lr_l = MATRIX_LR * (1 - 0.5 * l / (DEPTH - 1)), so layer 0 gets the full rate and the last layer gets half. Implement by giving each block's matrix tensors its own parameter group with the scaled lr while keeping the same momentum and weight decay. Leave embedding, lm_head and scalar groups unchanged.
backlog.title: Depth-scaled Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Build the attention mask so tokens cannot attend across document boundaries inside a packed training sequence: detect the BOS token id (or the document separator the loader already emits) and restrict attention to the current document via a block-diagonal causal mask combined with the existing sliding-window mask. Do not change the data loader or its names. If the window pattern uses fused flash attention without custom masks, implement this with a cumulative document-id comparison on the query and key indices and fall back to ignoring it if the kernel cannot accept a mask.
backlog.title: Attention masking at document boundaries

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention block and each MLP block (the matrices that write into the residual stream) with standard deviation 1/sqrt(2 * DEPTH * model_dim) instead of the default, while keeping all other init unchanged. This keeps the residual stream variance from growing with depth at the start of training. Apply the scale once at model construction; no change to the optimizer or schedule.
backlog.title: Scaled residual output initialization

backlog.spec: Apply rotary position embedding to only the first half of each head's dimensions and leave the second half unrotated, so some channels carry position-free content matching. Implement by slicing q and k into rotated and pass-through halves before the RoPE function and concatenating afterward. Keep the RoPE base, QK-norm and head count unchanged. This is a small code change in the attention forward and adds no parameters.
backlog.title: Partial rotary embedding on half the head dimensions

backlog.spec: Add a second embedding table of size 4096 (or 2^12) rows and dimension model_dim, zero-initialized. For each position t, compute a bigram index as (prev_token * 1000003 + cur_token) mod 4096, where prev_token is the token at t-1 (use 0 at position 0 of each sequence). Look up the bigram embedding and add it to the token embedding before the first RMSNorm and the first block. Train this table with the same Adam group and LR as the token embedding (EMBEDDING_LR). Do not add it to the lm_head. Everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Hashed bigram embedding added to token embedding

backlog.spec: After computing the token embeddings x (before the first block), form x_prev by shifting x one position to the right along the sequence axis, with a zero vector at position 0. Add a learnable per-channel gate g = sigmoid(w) with w initialized to a value giving g around 0.1 (a vector of size model_dim), and set x = x + g * x_prev. Put w in the scalar Adam group (SCALAR_LR). The shift must respect the sequence layout the dataloader uses; it only mixes positions within the same sequence. No other change.
backlog.title: Smear gate mixing previous-token embedding

backlog.spec: Create a second embedding table of the same vocabulary and dimension as the token embedding, initialized to zero. In the second half of the blocks (layers index >= DEPTH/2), add a learnable scalar-gated copy of this embedding of the current token to the value projection output v before attention, i.e. v = v + lambda_l * ve[token], with lambda_l a per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5 and kept in the scalar Adam group. Train the value-embedding table with EMBEDDING_LR in its own Adam group. The rest of attention (RoPE, QK-norm, window pattern) is unchanged.
backlog.title: Value embeddings injected into later-layer values

backlog.spec: In each Block, apply an extra RMSNorm to the output of the attention sublayer and to the output of the MLP sublayer before each is added to the residual stream. That is x = x + norm_post_attn(attn(norm_pre(x))) and x = x + norm_post_mlp(mlp(norm_pre(x))), with the post-norms having no learnable weight (or a learnable per-channel gain initialized to 1). Keep the existing pre-norms and the existing residual-scale scalars. This bounds the magnitude each sublayer writes into the residual stream.
backlog.title: Sandwich norm on sublayer outputs

backlog.spec: Tie the lm_head weight to the token embedding matrix (single shared parameter, so lm_head = embedding.T), and remove the separate UNEMBEDDING_LR Adam group, folding the shared matrix into the EMBEDDING_LR group. Use the parameters saved by the removed head to increase DEPTH by 1 so the total parameter budget and wall-clock stay roughly constant. Scale the tied embedding init to std 0.02 at start and keep the logit softmax path unchanged. Recompute model_dim from the new DEPTH using ASPECT_RATIO so head count and HEAD_DIM still divide evenly.
backlog.title: Tied input and output embeddings with one extra layer

backlog.spec: Replace each block's dense MLP with a top-1 mixture of 2 expert MLPs, each with hidden width halved so per-token FLOPs match the baseline. Add a linear router of size model_dim to 2 with no bias, and route each token to argmax expert, scaling the expert output by the softmax probability of the chosen expert. Add a Switch-style load-balancing auxiliary loss with coefficient 0.01 averaged over layers. Keep the squared-ReLU activation inside each expert. Experts are computed with a simple gather of tokens per expert, not a fused kernel.
backlog.title: Iso-compute mixture-of-experts MLP

backlog.spec: Set the training loss to cross-entropy with label smoothing epsilon = 0.02 over the full vocabulary (the smoothing mass is spread uniformly across all vocab entries, including the target). Leave the validation loss path untouched so the reported metric is the standard unsmoothed bits-per-byte. Implement via the built-in label_smoothing argument of the cross-entropy call used in the training forward pass only. No other change.
backlog.title: Label smoothing on the training cross-entropy

backlog.spec: In the Muon orthogonalization step, replace the quintic Newton-Schulz coefficients with the more conservative set (a, b, c) = (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) that converges to an exact polar factor rather than the aggressive oscillating set currently used. Keep the same number of iterations and the same momentum, LR, and weight decay. The goal is a smoother orthogonalized update that is less sensitive to the 300 s budget's late-training gradient scale.
backlog.title: More conservative Newton-Schulz coefficients in Muon

backlog.spec: Initialize the lm_head weight to exactly zero at model construction so the first logits are uniform and the initial loss equals log(vocab). Keep all other weight inits unchanged. Add a learnable scalar output multiplier s initialized to 1.0 in the scalar Adam group and multiply the final normed hidden state by s before the lm_head. This decouples the output scale from the Adam LR of the head and lets the optimizer set logit magnitude directly.
backlog.title: Zero-initialized lm_head with logit-scale warmup

backlog.spec: Set the initial value of each block's residual scale scalars (the attention and MLP residual multipliers already present) to 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH) instead of their current initialization, so the residual stream variance stays near constant as depth grows. Keep those scalars in the scalar Adam group at SCALAR_LR and leave the rest of the initialization unchanged. This is a small init-only change that matches the scaled residual initialization idea in principle while avoiding any change to the forward pass or the optimizer.
backlog.title: Layer-depth-scaled residual gains initialized to 1/sqrt(depth)

backlog.spec: During training only, add zero-mean Gaussian noise to the token embedding output x0 before the first block, with std = 0.1 times the RMS of x0 per token. Keep the noise off at evaluation. Draw noise with torch.randn_like under the existing training forward pass, adding no new parameters or config beyond one constant NOISE_STD = 0.1. The loss and targets are unchanged.
backlog.title: Gaussian noise on input embeddings during training

backlog.spec: During training, replace each input token with a dedicated mask id with probability 0.03 before the embedding lookup, while keeping the original tokens as the next-token targets. Use a Bernoulli mask from torch.rand; for the mask id, reuse an unused index or extend the embedding table by one row. Disable masking at evaluation. Keep the causal attention and the rest of the training loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Random input-token masking as light regularization

backlog.spec: Replace the DEPTH distinct transformer blocks with 2 unique blocks whose weights are shared, applied in the sequence A,B,A,B,... so the effective depth stays 8 applications. Keep the per-layer scalars and the window pattern indexed by applied layer, and keep the total parameter count near the baseline by widening model_dim only if the code path allows it. Otherwise keep the width fixed and accept fewer parameters. The forward pass and optimizer grouping must treat the shared weights as one parameter set.
backlog.title: Looped weight-shared block recurrence

backlog.spec: Skip the rotary position embedding in every fourth attention layer (layers 3 and 7 for DEPTH 8, zero-indexed 3 and 7), so those layers attend without positional rotation while the others keep RoPE. Keep the QK normalization, sliding-window masks and the value path unchanged. Change only the rotary application call for those layer indices, with no new hyperparameters beyond a NOPE_EVERY = 4 constant.
backlog.title: NoPE layers without rotary embedding

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed square in the MLP activation relu(x)^2 with relu(x)^p, where p is a learnable scalar per block initialized to 2.0 and stored as a float parameter, clamped to the range [1.0, 3.0] in the forward pass. Put p in the scalar Adam group with SCALAR_LR and no weight decay. Keep the rest of the MLP, its projections and initialization unchanged.
backlog.title: Learnable exponent in the squared-ReLU MLP

backlog.spec: Scale the Adam learning rates for the embedding, lm_head and scalar groups by (256 / model_dim) raised to the power 0.5, so the rates follow a width-aware rule when model_dim changes. Keep the Muon matrix LR unchanged and keep the base EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR and SCALAR_LR constants as the reference values at model_dim 256. Compute the scale once after the model is built and apply it to each param group's lr before training starts.
backlog.title: Width-scaled learning rates for Adam groups

backlog.spec: Maintain a running uniform average of the model parameters over the final 20% of the training time budget, updating it every 10 optimizer steps during that window. Start the average at the beginning of the last 20% of time, and after training finishes, copy the averaged parameters into the model before the final evaluation. Keep the normal training loop and the evaluation call unchanged, and store the average on the same device in bf16 to save memory.
backlog.title: Uniform tail averaging of checkpoints in the warmdown

backlog.spec: Compute the final cross-entropy loss over the sequence in chunks of 512 positions instead of materializing the full fp32 logits for the whole micro-batch. Each chunk takes its slice of hidden states, applies lm_head and the loss, and accumulates the sum before dividing by the token count, with backward flowing through each chunk. This removes the largest activation buffer, which allows DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 with the same total batch, halving gradient accumulation steps. Keep the loss value and the total batch size identical.
backlog.title: Chunked cross-entropy to free logits memory

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown multiplier with a square-root decay over the warmdown window: lr_mult = 1 - sqrt(progress), where progress goes from 0 at the start of the warmdown to 1 at the end, keeping WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5 and FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups, including Muon. The schedule is a single function of elapsed time fraction and changes nothing else in the loop.
backlog.title: Square-root cooldown in the warmdown

backlog.spec: Weight each target token's cross-entropy term by w = (f_t)^(-0.25) normalized so the mean weight over the batch equals 1, where f_t is the unigram frequency of token t estimated once from the first 100 training batches and stored as a fixed vector. This upweights rare tokens and downweights frequent ones without touching the byte-length weighting. Compute the weights once before training, keep the loss reduction a weighted mean, and leave evaluation on the unweighted metric.
backlog.title: Token-frequency reweighting of the loss

Hurt: tied lm_head (+1.7839), byte-weighted loss (+0.0635), cosine decay (+0.0617), sublayer RMSNorm (+0.0240), SwiGLU (+0.0104), parallel blocks (+0.0100). Neutral or worse: GQA, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7, Newton-Schulz coefficients (+0.0027), extra embedding table (+0.0024).
